findings.description: The user_data script exports AWS_ACCESS_KEY_ID and AWS_SECRET_ACCESS_KEY as plaintext static credentials. EC2 user data is retrievable from the instance metadata service by anyone who can reach the instance (e.g. via SSRF or shell access), and it is also stored in plaintext in the Terraform state and API describe calls.

Ingress rule allows TCP/22 from 0.0.0.0/0, exposing SSH to the entire internet for an instance that receives a public IP, enabling brute-force and direct remote attack on the administrative interface.
The egress rule permits all protocols and ports to 0.0.0.0/0, providing no outbound restriction and facilitating data exfiltration or command-and-control traffic from a compromised host.
Port 80 is open to 0.0.0.0/0 and the instance serves plain HTTP only (no TLS configured in user_data), so traffic to the web host is transmitted in cleartext.
The EBS volume is created without the encrypted argument set to true (it is explicitly commented out), so data stored on the attached volume is unencrypted at rest.
The snapshot is taken from an unencrypted volume and no encryption is specified, so the snapshot data is stored unencrypted and any accidental sharing exposes cleartext data.
The VPC flow log destination bucket has no server-side encryption configuration, so network flow records (which reveal internal topology and traffic patterns) are stored unencrypted.

No public access block, bucket ACL restriction, or bucket policy enforcing TLS is defined for the flow log bucket, leaving it reliant on account-level defaults to prevent public exposure of sensitive network logs.

map_public_ip_on_launch is true and the subnet routes to an internet gateway, so instances launched here — including the web host with SSH open to the world — are directly reachable from the internet with no bastion or NAT boundary.
map_public_ip_on_launch is true and the subnet is associated with a route table routing 0.0.0.0/0 to the internet gateway, so any workload placed here is automatically internet-exposed.

No metadata_options block enforcing http_tokens = "required", so IMDSv1 remains enabled; combined with a public-facing web server this allows SSRF-based theft of instance credentials and of the plaintext secrets embedded in user data.
No root_block_device with encrypted = true is specified, so the instance root volume — which will also contain the credentials written by user_data — is not encrypted at rest.
